font_base.description: The URL prefix under which the two faces are served, relative to the page's own base. Empty means no @font-face at all: the sheet's fallback stacks carry the type and the screen makes no request. The two file names are fixed -- inter.woff2 and fraunces.woff2 -- so what an operator provides is one directory, not a list. No font file ships in this repository.

description.purpose: The screen's whole bookkeeping, and it draws nothing itself: it validates a view, keeps `(owner, view_id)` unique by hand, computes what the display's object tree must therefore look like, and says so as one bundle of object calls.
description.use_when: Inside a display hive. It is the only cell that reads or writes the views table and the only one that patches the display.
description.not_in_scope: No model, no network, no clock but the wall clock. It owns no content -- the content is whatever the sender sent, rendered by whatever component the sender defined -- and it makes no layout judgement beyond two regions and an order: the `ord` a view declared, then its first appearance, ties broken on identity, and never the moment a view was last written. It owns no identity either: the owner of a view is the envelope's `reply_to`, and a body that names a different one is refused rather than believed.
examples: pass 1: a request on `in_view` / `in_withdraw` -> one store bundle, select then delete then insert, the request riding along on the hop
pass 1: a browser event -> the same event handed out of the hive with the owner and view_id its object id parses back to

pass 2: the store's answer -> the after-state computed in memory, expired views dropped, then one read of what the display already holds -- which carries the seats, so the read is an input to the layout and not only a diff
pass 3: the display's answer -> one bundle of object calls, or the whole bootstrap when the page is not ours
pass 4: the display's acknowledgement -> nothing, which is what stops the loop
